subject: artifacts/retention-tiers.v2.json

independence.method: Blindly derived the minimum durable proof for a positive match, a negative/no-match result, a relationship/set claim, a policy verdict, and a later replay before reading v2; then diffed those obligations against every retained field and conformance assertion.
independence.differentInstrument: The author repaired the known excerpt-versus-relationship examples. This review tests the unit of proof (finding versus evaluation/outcome), commitment versus witness bytes, adversarial shape declarations, and zero-finding Runs.

acceptedDirection: T1-excerpt is correctly withdrawn as a universal proof tier.
Local, path, and absence claims do require different witness shapes.
T0 now states that fact-relation bodies are not silently pinned; this removes the largest T0 custody ambiguity.
An immutable sealedTier plus separately derived current availability is the correct direction for B-RT-04; the sealed Run must not be rewritten.
Fail-loud policy for insufficient proof capability and no silent proof truncation are correct requirements.

decisionRecommendations.CD-RT-1: REJECT the current accept-as-default recommendation and require v3. Keep T1-proof as the design direction, but do not ship authoritative/gating persistence with T0 as a fallback: until a verifiable T1 exists and storage choice occurs before the first write, Runs must be explicitly ephemeral/advisory or the release remains incomplete.
decisionRecommendations.CD-RT-2: POSTPONE. T1-partition may be required, not optional, for absence and complete-set proofs; that cannot be decided until proof sufficiency and deduplication are specified and measured.
decisionRecommendations.CD-RT-3: ACCEPT IN DIRECTION. sealedTier stays immutable; availability belongs in a separate append-only retention/availability record. v3 must define per-proof granularity, permitted degradation events, and the conflict with retained-Run pinning.

priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-01: PARTIAL. v2 recognizes path and absence shapes, but the required payloads are commitments rather than independently checkable witnesses and the model omits no-finding/outcome proofs.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-02: MOSTLY CLOSED for T0 fact-body ambiguity: v2 says T0 retains identities/digests rather than full relation bodies. Coverage-body custody remains load-bearing for absence proofs.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-03: OPEN. The default remains underived: no complete proof-family matrix, executable verifier, representative size/privacy distribution, or resolution for unsupported/truncated proofs exists.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-04: CLOSED IN CONCEPT for the mutable-Run defect. sealedTier plus external effective availability is correct; the successor availability and pinning contract remains incomplete.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-05: OPEN. Proof size and source/PII cost remain unmeasured; absence and aggregate proofs may approach relation-partition scale.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-06: OPEN. T2 still claims full re-derivation and attestation while retaining input bytes and toolchain identities rather than the executable environment.
priorFindingDisposition.B-RT-07: PARTIAL. Excerpts are optional and privacy-classed, but v2 permits default T1 proof objects to retain them without a default-off rule, retention lifetime, or pre-write storage choice.

resolves.B-RTV2-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: FindingProof is the wrong proof unit; a clean/pass Run carries no proof of rule evaluations, no-match results, baseline comparison, or policy verdict.
resolves.B-RTV2-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: required local/path/absence fields are anchors and digests, not sufficient retained witnesses; well-typed T1 objects can remain unverifiable.
resolves.B-RTV2-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: rule-declared findingShape plus structural typing is producer self-attestation; no host-owned proof obligation or verifier validates semantic adequacy.
resolves.B-RTV2-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: truncation is allowed while T1 promises complete why; residualDigest cannot replace omitted witness data and terminal semantics are unspecified.
resolves.B-RTV2-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: T1-proof default is unmeasured and does not resolve V1/V2/V4/V5 before source-derived proof objects are written.
resolves.B-RTV2-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: reachability-based degradation conflicts with retained-Run evidence pinning and is too coarse to report per-evaluation proof availability.
resolves.B-RTV2-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: the shape taxonomy cannot express complete-set/aggregate, metric, policy/baseline, external-observation, and derivation claims; blast radius is reduced incorrectly to one membership path.
resolves.B-RTV2-08: OPEN-BLOCKER: T2 retains insufficient custody for its full-replay and attestation-grade claim.
resolves.B-RTV2-09: OPEN-BLOCKER: the proposed proof schema and tests are prose-only; no executable schema, independent verifier, or failing golden establishes conformance.

evidence: T1 retains a FindingProof `for each finding`; no other evaluation- or outcome-proof type exists.
A passing Run with zero findings therefore retains zero FindingProof objects and differs from T0 only by an empty proof collection.
The sealed domain model separates facts, findings, Coverage, and verdict; proving findings does not prove the policy verdict.
No proof records why an activated rule produced no match, why a baseline comparison produced no net-new finding, how waivers affected policy, or why required Coverage justified pass.
The artifact contains no EvaluationProof, VerdictProof, or no-finding proof concept.
findings.counterexample: Run a forbidden-dependency rule over a clean repository. findings=[] satisfies `noProofNoSeal` vacuously at T1-proof, yet a later reader has no retained witness that the dependency relation was exhaustively evaluated or that policy legitimately returned pass.
findings.impact: The tool's most important answer—no new violations—remains unexplained and uncheckable. A local per-finding form is promoted into a global claim that the Run is proven.
findings.requiredChange: Make the retained unit an EvaluationProof for every activated rule/query plus a VerdictDerivationProof. Positive findings carry nested witnesses; no-match evaluations carry exact predicate/rule identity, fact-view and Coverage commitments with retained verification material; baseline/waiver/policy steps carry their input identities and derivation. T1 may seal only when the complete outcome proof graph is valid.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A different mandatory T1 object already proving every no-match evaluation and the verdict, referenced by v2 but not named in this artifact.

evidence: A local proof requires only subjectAnchors; source/context/metric inputs are optional. A content-relative span identity cannot show why a forbidden API or large-function threshold matched after bytes are gone.
A path proof requires edge identities and endpoints; its edge description requires evidence digests, not the evidence bodies or authenticated membership witnesses needed to check each edge.

An absence proof requires coverageDigest, relation, and roots. T0 already retains Coverage digests/outcomes, while architecture/04 says the exact Coverage manifest can be fact-partition-sized and is stored behind that digest.
A digest commits to unseen data; it does not demonstrate membership, non-membership, exhaustive traversal, or predicate evaluation.
t0FactBodies says needed fact bodies may be embedded or referenced, but proofSchema does not require those bodies or require references to remain reachable.
findings.counterexample: A `large-function` finding with only a file/span hash is well typed as local and can seal at T1, but the retained object contains neither the measured size nor the body/normalized facts from which the threshold can be checked. An absence proof containing only a Coverage root has the same defect for zero references.
findings.impact: T1 objects may identify the assertion without carrying evidence sufficient to verify it. The design renames references and commitments as proof while still losing the why after GC.
findings.requiredChange: For every proof obligation, specify the retained witness body or an authenticated membership/non-membership proof and deterministic verifier. Local proofs retain predicate inputs or canonical fact/source witness; path proofs retain checkable edge provenance; absence proofs retain the exact Coverage certificate body plus a verifiable closed-set/non-membership witness. Required object references enter the sealed manifest and remain reachable for the promised lifetime.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A normative definition that `proof` means only a non-verifiable human explanation. That would require withdrawing the product constraint that the answer can be established later.

evidence: Each rule/profile declares its own findingShape.
The seal rule checks that exactly one proof is well typed and its kind matches that declaration.
No verifier identity, verifier version, validation algorithm, or host-owned mapping from evaluator semantics to proof obligation exists.
A buggy or adversarial relationship rule can declare local and satisfy T1 with a span anchor.
findings.impact: The producer whose conclusion needs proof also chooses the easiest proof class and attests that its own output satisfies it. Structural validity is mistaken for semantic validity.
findings.requiredChange: Make proof obligations host-owned, versioned, and bound to the evaluator/rule contract. Record ProofObligationId and VerifierId/version in PlanId and the sealed proof graph. Validate proofs through an independent deterministic verifier path with mutation cases that a producer-generated but semantically false witness fails.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A contribution admission contract outside this artifact that independently reviews and enforces the declaration against executable proof-verifier tests for every gate-authoritative rule.

evidence: RT-6 and noProofNoSeal say a T1 Run cannot seal without a well-typed proof for every finding.
RT-7 says proof-budget exhaustion is Coverage/diagnostic rather than silent truncation.
bounds nevertheless permits FindingProof truncation=true plus residualDigest and only instructs consumers not to treat it as complete.
An SCC member list may be cut at 32 and replaced by a digest of omitted members, which cannot explain or verify a claim about the complete set.
No lifecycle, Coverage, verdict, tier-downgrade, or finding-authority result is specified for this case.
findings.impact: The same Run can be labelled T1-proof while its own contract says the proof is incomplete. Different consumers can gate, display, or reject the same truncated finding differently.
findings.requiredChange: Define claim-specific sufficiency. If the authoritative claim needs omitted data, proof exhaustion makes the evaluation indeterminate or prevents T1 seal; a digest is not a substitute. If a bounded witness proves only a narrower claim (for example one cycle exists), emit that narrower claim and keep aggregate/member-count claims separate. Add exact D9/Coverage outcomes for exhaustion.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A rule that every truncatable proof's authoritative claim is fully established by the retained prefix alone, with the omitted data explicitly excluded from the claim semantics.

evidence: V1 and V2 are critical because the tool writes source-derived/PII-bearing copies to a location and lifetime the user did not choose, often under sync/backup software.
T1-proof is default and may retain identifiers, edge structures, fact bodies, and bounded source excerpts; privacy classification inventories the copy but does not prevent creating it.
defaultAndDisclosure states first-run disclosure but does not make safe-root resolution, sync-root refusal, retention duration, or a storage/tier choice a precondition before the first proof write.
Threat V5 requires a stated default lifetime and real deletion; v2 specifies neither duration nor deletion semantics.
Proof budgets and size labels are judgment; absence/complete-set evidence can require the exact Coverage manifest, which architecture/04 says may approach fact-partition size.
The clean-sheet comparison and representative size/privacy measurement have not run.
findings.impact: Accepting T1-proof as default can resolve the explainability problem by silently recreating the high-severity user-copy problem. The cost may approach T1-partition/T2 for the rule families used to justify the default.
findings.requiredChange: Before any persistent proof write, resolve and display the exact storage root, refuse unsafe/sync-managed roots, inventory projected data classes/size, and let the user choose durable T1/T2 or explicit ephemeral/advisory operation. State default lifetimes and deletion behavior. Measure deduplicated proof size and privacy classes on representative workloads before ratifying a universal default.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A binding admission/storage contract that runs before the first write and already supplies those guarantees, plus representative evidence that proof storage remains materially below replay custody.

evidence: The sealedTier/current-availability separation correctly avoids mutating a Run.
architecture/06 says evidence objects referenced by retained Runs are pinned by ledger reachability.
v2 simultaneously describes GC deleting FindingProof bytes while the retained Run remains sealed as T1-proof.
effectiveExplainability is one Run-level value even when one finding proof, one optional excerpt, one Coverage body, or one T2 input may be missing independently.
The store state does not distinguish explicit purge, policy expiry, corruption, temporary unavailability, or partial-object loss.
findings.impact: Consumers cannot know which exact claim remains checkable or whether loss was authorized. Automatic GC can break a retained manifest reference contrary to the existing pinning invariant.
findings.requiredChange: Commit the required proof-object inventory in the immutable Run/Evidence manifest. Track per-evaluation/per-object availability and loss reason in a separate append-only retention ledger or tombstone. Retained authoritative Runs pin required proof objects until an explicit policy expiry/purge transition; ordinary cache GC cannot degrade them. Derive a Run summary from those granular states.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A definition that every retained Run ceases to be retained at the same atomic transition that unpins its proof graph, with typed tombstone resolution preserving the loss reason.

evidence: The taxonomy offers local, path, absence, and an unspecified composite list.
Blast radius as a whole is a complete reachable set/cardinality claim, not merely proof that one member has one path.
Large-function is a metric/threshold derivation, not established by a local subject anchor.
Policy verdicts, baseline differences, aggregate counts, similarity/clone scores, external scanner observations, and Probe results have no proof kind or aggregation operator.
Composite lists sub-proofs but does not encode the deterministic derivation combining them into the claimed value.
findings.impact: Many shipped or planned result families either cannot seal at T1 or will be forced into a weaker shape that does not prove their actual claim.
findings.requiredChange: Derive proof obligations from all evaluator/result families. Add at least derivation/metric, complete-set/aggregate, external-observation, and policy/baseline forms, each with exact claim semantics and verifier. Treat composite as a typed derivation DAG, not an unstructured list.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A proof that each omitted family is encoded losslessly by an existing kind, including its aggregate/threshold operation and verification algorithm.

evidence: T2 retains all read-set bytes plus Plan/toolchain identities.
It does not require retrievable producer/provider binaries, rule IR, schemas, compiler/sysroot/package/database artifacts, environment realization, or a supported replay executor.
An identity proves what was used; it does not make that historical executable artifact available offline.
The tier nevertheless promises full re-derivation and attestation grade.
findings.impact: A user can pay the full source-retention privacy cost and discover later that the promised replay is impossible because the execution environment is gone.
findings.requiredChange: Rename T2 to input-complete unless it pins or guarantees retrieval of the complete executable derivation closure and defines a deterministic replay verifier. State attestation trust/signature requirements separately from replayability.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A binding delivery/versioning contract guaranteeing offline retrieval and execution of every identity in the historical Plan for the stated retention period.

evidence: proofSchema is explicitly logical; field-level encoding is a known limitation.
conformanceTests are English assertions with no payload goldens or executable verifier.
There is no schema validation for required references, shape/claim compatibility, digest closure, or availability state.
No failing cases cover a clean Run with no proofs, a forged edge, a missing Coverage body, a misdeclared shape, incomplete truncation, or deleted required proof bytes.
findings.impact: The artifact cannot yet demonstrate that any implementation—or even a concrete example object—satisfies its load-bearing claims. It is a useful design sketch, not a closable contract.
findings.requiredChange: v3 must include a concrete versioned schema, canonicalization/digest rules, proof-verifier interface, outcome-proof graph, and executable positive/negative goldens authored or reviewed independently from the schema author.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separately retained executable conformance artifact already referenced by v2 and covering these negative cases.

counterexamples.inputs: one activated forbidden-dependency rule, complete declared Coverage, zero findings, pass verdict
counterexamples.v2SealResult: allowed by the per-finding noProofNoSeal rule
counterexamples.expected: a retained no-match EvaluationProof and VerdictDerivationProof

counterexamples.inputs: large-function finding with subjectAnchors but no body, metric, or predicate inputs
dead-code finding with subject, relation, roots, and coverageDigest but no exact Coverage body/non-membership witness
counterexamples.expected: reject as a commitment without proof of exhaustive absence

counterexamples.inputs: relationship rule declares local and emits one subject anchor
SCC/member-set claim exceeds 32 members; retained prefix plus residualDigest
counterexamples.v2SealResult: truncated proof representable; terminal effect unspecified
counterexamples.expected: narrow the claim or make evaluation indeterminate/prevent T1 seal

sealedPropertiesCovered: architecture/01 product constraint — results are checkable later and prove the answer
architecture/02 plane separation — facts, findings, Coverage, and verdict require distinct derivation evidence
architecture/02 EvidenceDigest — immutable canonical sealed manifest
architecture/04 Coverage artifact — exact membership, predicate IR, and set commitment rather than summary
architecture/06 evidence-object reachability — retained Runs pin required evidence
threat-model.v2 V1/V2/V4/V5/V10 — minimise source-derived copies, safe storage root, excerpt handling, stated retention/deletion, and explainability conflict
knownLimitations: This review specifies proof obligations, not a chosen authenticated-set or cryptographic proof construction.
No representative proof-size dataset exists, so the review rejects categorical default/size claims rather than supplying replacement numbers.
It does not inspect current implementation code because retention-tiers.v2 is a greenfield contract and makes no load-bearing claim about existing runtime behavior.
Reviewer A authored the subject artifact; no Reviewer-A review artifact or note comparison was used.
